message.content:
Los Angeles (Pacific Time) is normally **9 hours behind** Berlin (Central European Time).  
However, because the U.S. and Europe change daylight‑saving time on slightly different dates, the gap can shift:

| Period | Los Angeles | Berlin | Time Difference |
|--------|-------------|--------|-----------------|
| Standard time in both zones | UTC‑8 | UTC+1 | **9 h** |
| U.S. on DST, Europe on standard | UTC‑7 | UTC+1 | **8 h** |
| Both on DST | UTC‑7 | UTC+2 | **9 h** |
| U.S. on standard, Europe on DST | UTC‑8 | UTC+2 | **10 h** |

So, for most of the year the difference is 9 hours, but during the brief overlap windows (early March and early November) it can be 8 hours or 10 hours. If you need the exact difference for a specific date, let me know!

During daylight saving time, PT is UTC-7, CEST is UTC+2, difference is 9 hours. Actually both shift by one hour, so difference remains 9 hours. In Europe, DST starts last Sunday in March, ends last Sunday in October. So there is a period from March to early March where the difference might be 8 hours? After US DST starts, Los Angeles is UTC-7, Berlin is still UTC+1 until last Sunday in March. So difference is 8 hours. Then after Berlin DST starts, Berlin is UTC+2, Los Angeles is UTC-7 until first Sunday in November. So difference is 9 hours. After Berlin DST ends, Berlin is UTC+1, Los Angeles is UTC-7 until first Sunday in November. So difference is 8 hours. So the difference changes between 8 and 9 hours depending on DST overlap.
